title: JSON asset lookup error boundary for governed execution writeback

phases.objective: Preserve the original provider failure and complete governed execution evidence when JSON Asset Registry reconciliation is unavailable.

e2e_journeys.actor: System tool dispatcher recording a failed GitHub provider execution
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: performUniversalServerWriteback with a failed github_get_git_ref_head result and an unavailable JSON Asset Registry lookup
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The original provider error remains authoritative, the execution log and JSON asset evidence are written, and the secondary registry lookup failure is emitted only as a bounded warning.
steps: Submit a failed GitHub provider result to the universal writeback orchestration with SQL runtime authority.
Force JSON Asset Registry reconciliation to throw the missing governed spreadsheet identifier error.
Continue the governed writeback path and persist execution-log and JSON-asset evidence.
Read back the returned writeback state and captured warning to verify that the provider failure was not masked.
assertions: The returned status, error code, and short message remain the original provider failure values.
Exactly one Execution Log Unified row is written with failed status.
A JSON asset row is still written even though prior-asset lookup failed.
The governed pre-response log guard remains passed.
The missing spreadsheet identifier appears only in the bounded warning and does not replace the provider result.

phases.objective: Add structured observability and alert classification for degraded secondary writeback dependencies without changing provider authority.
Exercise additional registry, storage, and execution-log dependency failures while proving bounded continuation and deterministic evidence.
Validate the same failure boundary against a live non-production SQL-authoritative runtime.
Verify exact Production SHA and runtime readback without intentionally disrupting production dependencies.
